title: Try the nearest example
summary: A nearest-neighbour rule uses the closest stored example. Distance tells us how far two values are apart. Here distance is the size of their difference.
introduction: A nearest-neighbour rule uses the closest stored example. Distance tells us how far two values are apart. Here distance is the size of their difference. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A nearest-neighbour rule uses the closest stored example. Distance tells us how far two values are apart. Here distance is the size of their difference.

blocks.code:
examples = [(1, "small"), (3, "small"), (8, "large")]
query = 7
nearest = min(examples, key=lambda row: abs(row[0] - query))
print(nearest[1])
blocks.title: Try the nearest example

blocks.text: The output is large. Distances from 7 are 6, 4 and 1, so the example at 8 is closest. min chooses the pair with the smallest distance.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use query 2 and notice that a tie needs a rule.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: One nearby example may be noisy or wrong; it is not enough evidence for a serious decision.
For more detail later, use this [Machine Learning further reading](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course).
